iMobileSitter protects passwords, PINs and TAN lists using an innovative technique that offers higher security than conventional password managers. At the same time, iMobileSitter is as easy to use as conventional products. Hackers get nuts due to iMobileSitter's resistance against typical attacks (e.g., dictionary and brute-force attacks). Such attacks use trial and error to find the correct master password. Technologies like cloud computing allow to tremendously speed-up these attacks. Hackers do not even have expert knowledge to run the attacks. Many of these supposed secure password managers are actually easy prey for hackers, even if they use strong encryption algorithms such as AES, since important security assumptions for using these algorithms have been neglected by conventional products. iMobileSitter is different. Here, strong cryptographic algorithms are applied in such way that hackers do not get any usable feedback. Thus, when using iMobileSitter the stored passwords are secure. 

Besides a higher security level, iMobileSitter provides additional features such as secure random password generation and a backup and restore function to provide additional reliability of the stored secrets in case of defect, loss, or theft. iMobileSitter combines higher security with convenience functions and easy to use interface.

iMobileSitter was developed by the Fraunhofer Institute for Secure Information Technology SIT in Germany. 


SECURITY

iMobileSitter provides resistance against dictionary and brute force attacks. Nowadays, hackers usually test huge amounts of possible master passwords in order to get to the stored secrets. When using conventional password managers to encrypt data, a hacker can detect if the attempted attack was successful even without the necessity of testing the decryption result as a password at the respective service. 

iMobileSitter is different. Here, an attacker cannot decide if the attempt was successful when looking at the decryption results. iMobileSitter accepts all master passwords. It decrypts the stored information on the basis of the given master password, irrespective of whether or not it is correct. However, the software misguides attackers by displaying wrong passwords.

Every decryption result looks as if it could be correct. For example, if a hacker decrypts a PIN assigned to a debit card using a master password, the decryption result that is returned will always be a four-digit number combination. From an attacker’s point of view - no matter whether hacker or hacking software - it is indistinguishable if the correct master password is found or not. For hacker or hacking software every decryption attempt seems to be successful.

To determine whether a decryption result is correct, the hacker has no choice but try to login with result at the respective service. There, however, additional security mechanisms of the service take effect after a defined amount of failed logins, e.g., three in the case of a debit card. 

Further information can be found on http://www.imobilesitter.com

SEAT THEM has 4 main objectives:
* Seating plans for all classes in all rooms
* Overview of attendance and participation
* A well-founded assessment basis for participation grades 
* Reduce the tedious paperwork as a class teacher.
=> this is exactly what Seat them is for.

TEACHING SUPPORT - Capture tables quickly and easily
In the course of a lesson, there are various little things that need to be recorded by the teacher, e.g. attendance, homework, parent signatures, book money, etc., but also class participation, disruptions, etc., if applicable. All of this has to be done quickly and intuitively, as lessons sometimes leave no time for documentation. The app contains examples of aspects that you can largely adapt to your needs:

Beginning of the lesson
At the start of the lesson, in addition to the presence of the students, it may also be necessary to record the extent to which homework and teaching materials are available: A swipe upwards on Peter and his forgotten homework is noted. A swipe to the left and the missed lesson is recorded. And if a student arrives late to class after all, a second swipe to the left is enough and the missed lesson is recorded in the table as a late arrival. 

Lessons
Whether it's about participation grades or well-founded feedback for parent-teacher conferences - SEAT THEM allows you to record three different values for students, e.g. active participation, disruption of lessons, etc., which can be freely defined. With each swipe, the counter for the corresponding student is increased and the associated color bar becomes more intense. This allows you to see at a glance who has been recorded more or less frequently.

Class management
As a class teacher, you have to record in various lists whether all monies/signatures/declarations etc. have been submitted. Four such lists can be managed individually for each class with simple swipe gestures. The color bars provide a quick overview of who still has something outstanding.

... and of course seating plans for your cell phone
Knowing the names of the pupils is the first hurdle for many colleagues; this is where a seating plan helps. But once you know the names, the seating plan is the fastest way to find individual students - faster than any table or list; notes can be made for each student in the seating plan using swipe gestures: Attendance, missing homework, class participation and much more.

Room planning
Rooms can be created in the app with their respective table arrangements. The grid can be expanded as required, tables with 1 or 2 desks can be arranged as required and rotated in 90° increments.

Student planning
In student planning, classes can be created and assigned the corresponding students, who can be placed in the created rooms simply by dragging and dropping.

In addition:
Exportable tables are created in the program for each pupil, which contain the corresponding counter values for each lesson. You can also correct these in the table. You can create an individual overview of the recorded data for each pupil.

Text annotations can be recorded for each pupil in each lesson, either because of a fantastic performance or because of an unpleasant incident. The times when a student left class are entered in this text file by the app.

User authentication and AES256 encryption
